en: Mayon Volcano has steep slopes because its highly viscous lava cools quickly and piles up near the vent instead of flowing far.
The Puerto Princesa Underground River formed because slightly acidic rainwater slowly dissolved the surrounding limestone rock over millions of years.
The Habagat monsoon brings heavy rain because moist winds from the West Philippine Sea drop water when hitting mountain ranges.
Main Lake Taal occupies a large caldera because a massive ancient volcanic eruption emptied the magma chamber, causing the ground to collapse.
The Cagayan River forms a wide delta at its mouth because slowing water drops its heavy sediment load into the ocean.
Tubbataha Reef grew massive because millions of tiny coral polyps continuously secreted hard calcium carbonate skeletons that stacked upon older layers.
Mount Apo features mossy forests because frequent cloud cover traps constant moisture, allowing thick mosses and epiphytes to thrive on trees.
The Banaue Rice Terraces prevent severe soil erosion because their carved stone walls hold the soil in place on steep mountain slopes.
Boracay has famous white sand because waves continuously break down and erode surrounding coral reefs into fine, powdery calcium carbonate grains.
Geothermal plants in Tiwi generate electricity because underground magma heats groundwater into steam, which then spins turbines to produce electrical power.
Camiguin island has many volcanoes because repeated historical eruptions from multiple volcanic vents continuously piled up new lava layers.
The Amihan brings cool, dry air to the Philippines because high pressure systems from Siberia push cold northeastern winds across the Asian landmass.
